top.title: UTSA vs. Tulsa: 5 players to watch as Roadrunners look to secure home field for American championship
top.description: UTSA Roadrunners quarterback Owen McCown runs the ball in a game against South Florida at the Alamodome in San Antonio, Texas on Thursday, Oct. 8, 2026. (Katina Zentz/San Antonio Express-News) After UTSA survived with a 19-17 win last week against UAB , coach Jeff Traylor's first instinct was to shield quarterback Owen McCown from the cameras and microphones. McCown hit just 12 of 20 passes for 112 yards with an interception in the win, marking a second straight quiet week after he threw for 85 yards with no touchdowns and an interception in the previous game against North Texas. The combined total of 197 passing yards is the lowest in any two-game stretch across McCown's three years as the Roadrunners starter. Though he acknowledged McCown "wasn't as sharp as he's been," Traylor also understood that quarterbacks shoulder an outsized portion of the credit or blame for the offensive performance, with many observers overlooking the protection issues or struggles at receiver that sometimes make McCown's life more challenging. But despite Traylor's instinct to allow McCown a moment out of the spotlight, McCown volunteered for a trip to the postgame interview room, facing the media before he'd even had time to change out of his cleats. "He's a man of ownership," Traylor said. "He's a tough, tough young man. For him to stand in front of the media and say that, I wasn't even going to let y'all have him, but he wanted to own it. That's just who that dude is, man. He's a stud." READ MORE: What UTSA's Jeff Traylor said about the coaching vacancy at TCU McCown called the opening half against the Blazers "my worst half of football I've ever played," marred by an interception deep in Roadrunners' territory that allowed UAB to punch in a tying touchdown just before halftime. But after watching UTSA's defense carry the team to a victory, McCown said he felt encouraged about the prospect of learning and building from those mistakes. "It was really just me hurting myself," McCown said. "It was uncharacteristic to me. I won't ever play a half like that again. It was rare for me. I had a couple of missed throws. I thought the reads were right, just wasn't going my way, and that'll happen. It's a full team game, though. And we came out with the win, so it's a lot easier to learn from." top.title: One year after Ji'Ayir Brown's curious claim of elite status, 49ers safety sounds prophetic
top.description: San Francisco 49ers safety Ji'Ayir Brown celebrates after a play against the Minnesota Vikings in the second half Sunday in Mexico City. (Gregory Payan/Associated Press) Last year, when Ji'Ayir Brown was one of the San Francisco 49ers ' backup safeties, he declared he was a top-five player at the position in the NFL. That prompted a logical - if slightly uncomfortable - follow-up question: How could he be among the league's best at his position if his own coaches didn't think he was one of the top two safeties on the roster? Brown didn't hesitate: "It's going to make sense one day." At the time, Brown sounded delusional. At the moment, he's looking prescient. After being benched in each of the previous two seasons, the 2023 third-round pick is enjoying a career-best year in which he ranks ninth among NFL safeties who have played at least 300 snaps, according to Pro Football Focus' grading system. Brown was already undramatically silencing social-media critics he'd acquired during his early career inconsistencies before he made a loud statement in the Niners' 35-10 win over the Vikings on Sunday in Mexico City. With the 49ers leading 21-10 just before halftime, Brown had an 18-yard interception return for a touchdown that signaled the rout was on. Asked about the pick-six, head coach Kyle Shanahan began by referencing Brown's up-and-down career. "Tig's been here for a while with us," Shanahan said, referring to Brown by his nickname. "He's been through a lot with us." The 49ers selected Brown No. 87 overall in 2023 when he was the draft's only player who had at least 10 interceptions over his final two college seasons. The Penn State standout then became a productive fill-in starter as a rookie and intercepted a Patrick Mahomes' pass in the 49ers' overtime loss to the Chiefs in Super Bowl LVIII. However, Brown had just five picks in his first 58 games before Sunday. Last year, he termed himself a "ball hawk," but acknowledged the big plays had been slow to come in the NFL. Last Sunday, however, Brown made a massive play because he was quick to diagnose QB Kirk Cousins' intentions. Lined up near the right hashmark, Brown took two steps to his left, toward the middle of the field, before Cousins took the shotgun snap. At the snap, Brown began running in the same direction while reading Cousins' eyes, which were locked onto wide receiver Tai Felton. Brown stepped in front of Felton, secured the pick and began an untouched jog into the end zone. Brown noted the 49ers faced Cousins in a 38-17 win over the Raiders on Nov. 8, two days before Cousins was traded to Minnesota. "I watched his tape a lot and picked up his mannerisms," Brown said. "I was in the right call to be in the right position." top.title: Why Texas A&M snub worked out for UTSA's Jeff Traylor
top.description: UTSA Roadrunners head coach Jeff Traylor looks on during the first quarter against the Rice Owls in Houston, Texas, Saturday, Oct., 3, 2026. (Zach Del Bello/San Antonio Express-News) Texas A&M did Jeff Traylor a favor. Three years ago, the Aggies interviewed him for an office that eventually makes every occupant miserable, then offered it to Mike Elko instead. Sure, the money would have been nice. But as you watch the men on the sidelines in College Station and San Antonio this Friday, ask yourself: Would you rather have Elko's options right now, or Traylor's? In some ways, they're still in completely different college football worlds. The same day that close to 110,000 people will file into Kyle Field to watch Elko's Aggies try to knock off No. 5 Texas, UTSA will be ecstatic to draw a crowd a third of that size to its regular-season finale at the Alamodome. But that disparity in attention comes with a disparity in expectations, and one of A&M's biggest problems is that it's never figured out the right ratio of the latter to the former. It's been almost three decades since the Aggies last won a conference championship, and 16 years since they've even played for one, and still every time they fall short of contention, it's a crisis. Setting high standards for your coaches is great. But once a fifth or sixth accomplished coach in a row fails to meet them, it might be fair to wonder if there's a difference between what your donor base calls standards and what outsiders call pipe dreams. It's not that coaches can't win at A&M. Kevin Sumlin and Jimbo Fisher managed one Top 5 finish apiece during their six-year tenures, and Elko came close last season. With the Aggies' money, resources and recruiting base, their competitive ceiling remains undeniably high. Their competitive floor, though, is lower than they ever like to acknowledge, and that was true even before a move to the Southeastern Conference made that more obvious. R.C. Slocum, Dennis Franchione and Mike Sherman each endured at least one losing Big 12 season after the Aggies won that league in 1998. UTSA Roadrunners head coach Jeff Traylor after the game against the Rice Owls in Houston, Texas, Saturday, Oct., 3, 2026. (Zach Del Bello/San Antonio Express-News) In the SEC, though, everybody has money, resources and a recruiting base, which reduces the margin for error and increases the likelihood of a crash like A&M's in 2026. Less than 12 months after taking the Aggies to the College Football Playoff, Elko is in danger of becoming the first coach in program history to lose eight conference games in one season. This isn't to say Traylor would have been doomed to the same predicament had the Aggies hired him after his 90-minute Zoom interview in 2023 . top.title: ‘Everything we need’ – Arteta encouraged by Gyokeres’ performance against Dortmund
top.description: ‘Everything we need’ – Arteta encouraged by Gyokeres’ performance against Dortmund Mikel Arteta says Viktor Gyokeres’ performance against Borussia Dortmund provides plenty of encouragement after the striker scored his side’s only goal. Gyokeres produced a superb finish to open the scoring after being awarded a start, having struggled to break into Arteta’s starting 11 so far this season. And the Arsenal boss was equally impressed by the striker’s all-round contribution to his side’s performance. “I think he had a brilliant performance today,” Arteta said. “I think he scored an unbelievable goal, he has the quality to do that. “What I loved the most was how connected he was to the team. We used him many times in different ways, his link-up play, the way he holds the ball, the way he threads it in behind and stretches the pitch. “There was a lot to like in that performance and that’s everything that we need.” Arteta was also pleased with Arsenal’s overall display against Dortmund but felt his side should have taken more from the chances they created. “A brilliant performance,” he said. “The way we played, bearing in mind the opposition that we played today, to do what we’ve done out there is something to be very, very pleased with. “There’s very little more you can demand from the team, but obviously the feeling is that we should have rewarded ourselves much more when you put that kind of performance in with the amount of chances.”

top.title: Why Eagles’ Vic Fangio is sure Jonathan Greenard’s ankle injury is behind him, even if he’s banged up
top.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Why Eagles’ Vic Fangio is sure Jonathan Greenard’s ankle injury is behind him, even if he’s banged up appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Through the first eight weeks of the 2026 NFL season, the Philadelphia Eagles ’ decision to trade and extend Jonathan Greenard looked like a Bryce Huff-level mistake by Howie Roseman . Coming off a down season due to injuries, Greenard suffered an injury over the summer that caused him to miss the first two weeks of the season. When he did return, Greenard looked more like his 2025 self than his double-digit sack seasons from 2023-24, recording just two tackles, zero tackles for a loss, and zero sacks. However, over the past two weeks – with a bye in between them – Greenard appears to finally be back to 100 percent, recording four tackles, two tackles for a loss, and two sacks a game during the team’s recent defensive resurgence. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Discussing Greenard’s recent resurgence over the past few weeks, Vic Fangio joked that it sure looks like Greenard is back to 100 percent, even if he’s still working back to 100 percent with continued treatment. “Hopefully. I told him, I said [ jokingly. ], he’s had a sack in each of the last two games, and that sack dance or celebration that he does afterwards indicates to me that there’s nothing wrong with his ankle, so he shouldn’t even be getting any treatment anymore. But that is not the case. He’s not 100% yet.” Fangio also commented on the Eagles’ resurgent pass rush, which has amassed more sacks in the last two weeks (11) than in their first eight games of the season (10). While some may point to Greenard’s health or the emerging narrative that Jordan Davis was holding the pass rush back as a run-stuffing 2-tech, Fangio admitted he doesn’t really know, but he’s happy the production has finally matched the effort level. “I don’t know. Other than — I’ve been telling you guys that it would come, but you didn’t believe me,” Fangio said. “But the guy we’re playing this week, I think, is the hardest guy in the league to sack. I think they have the best sack percentage for an offense of not getting sacked.” Could the Eagles’ pass-rushing issues really come down to getting their best players healthy? Will a healthy Greenard, plus an ascending Nolan Smith, and a more pass-rushing-centric nose tackle like Byron Young suddenly allow the Eagles to average five sacks per game down the stretch? Only time will tell, but as Fangio noted, their next challenge against the Cowboys on Thanksgiving will be incredibly telling either way. top.title: Alexandersson a contender for Swansea job
top.description: Freyr Alexandersson has only been in charge at current club Rosenborg since June [Getty Images] Freyr Alexandersson has emerged as a contender to take charge at Swansea City following the shock exit of Vitor Matos. Interim boss Ashley Williams led Swansea for the second time as they were beaten 2-1 at Middlesbrough on Tuesday. But the club have spoken to a number of candidates over the head coach vacancy and Rosenborg boss Alexandersson is thought to be a frontrunner. After falling to a fifth defeat in seven matches despite a battling performance at Boro, Swansea now turn their attention to Sunday's south Wales derby against Cardiff City. As it stands, there is no certainty over whether a new coaching team will be in place for the Cardiff game. When asked whether clarity is needed as Swansea prepare to face their rivals, Williams said: "That's not for me to comment on. "My job was to get the boys ready for this game [at Middlesbrough] and I did the best I could do. Now my job will be to debrief this game and take it from there. "I know you want an answer but I can't give it to you because I have got work to do about this game first and foremost. We'll look at the weekend when the time comes I think." Icelander Alexandersson, 44, has only been in charge of Rosenborg since June. The Norwegian top-flight club were in relegation danger when he was appointed, but lie fourth with just three games remaining in the season, which concludes in mid-December. Alexandersson previously worked for another Norwegian side, Brann, but was sacked earlier this year after 15 months in charge. Prior to that, he was manager of Belgian side Kortrijk, who are a sister club of Cardiff. "It's no secret when I spoke to Kortrijk I also had a conversation with the management of Cardiff that I'm going to train in England, to be a manager in the Championship or Premier League," Alexandersson said at the time. "There are big dreams and I realise that. It would be great if it was Cardiff. I would love to coach Cardiff at some point." top.title: Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund: The tactics board - How Niko Kovac's 53-clearance wall broke Mikel Arteta's 30-shot siege
top.description: Arsenal FC v Borussia Dortmund - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 - Getty Images Sport Arsenal dropped points at home in the Champions League league phase for the first time since the format was introduced, as Borussia Dortmund came from behind to draw 1-1 at the Emirates Stadium. On paper, the hosts were dominant. They had 63% of the ball, took 30 shots worth 2.34 expected goals (xG) and had 56 touches inside the Dortmund box. Yet both sides created four big chances, both had four shots on target, and Dortmund were the better team for long spells after the break. Viktor Gyokeres' long-range opener rewarded Arsenal's fast start, but Maximilian Beier's equaliser, made by a surging run from centre-back Joane Gadou, showed exactly where Arsenal were vulnerable. Arsenal's tactical setup Mikel Arteta lined up in a 4-2-3-1, with Declan Rice and Myles Lewis-Skelly in midfield behind Noni Madueke, Martin Odegaard and Christos Tzolis, and Gyokeres leading the line. Arsenal flew out of the blocks. Their press gave Dortmund no time on the ball in the opening 15 minutes, they completed 91% of their passes in the first half, and the opener arrived in the 10th minute when Madueke laid the ball into the path of Gyokeres, who sent a dipping 25-yard strike past Gregor Kobel. The right flank was Arsenal's main source of creativity. Madueke repeatedly got the better of Daniel Svensson , and he and Odegaard became the first Arsenal pair on record to create four or more chances each in a Champions League first half. On the other side, Piero Hincapie pushed high from left-back, joining attacks and even arriving at the back post for a header that Kobel saved early in the second half. The problem was the quality of Arsenal's chances. Eight of their 14 first-half shots came from outside the box, and the goal itself was worth just 0.03 xG. Set pieces made up 0.56 of their 0.94 first-half xG, and Madueke failed to bring down a rebound with the goal at his mercy in the 15th minute. Rice was the most dangerous runner from midfield, curling just over from distance in the 33rd minute and being denied by Nico Schlotterbeck's recovery tackle when through on goal two minutes later. Borussia Dortmund's tactical setup Niko Kovac set up with a back three of Gadou, Waldemar Anton and Schlotterbeck, with Julian Ryerson and Svensson as wing-backs, Felix Nmecha and Joey Veerman in central midfield, and Jobe Bellingham and Beier supporting Fabio Silva in attack. After a difficult opening quarter of an hour, Dortmund settled, won more of the midfield duels and began to look dangerous from set pieces, where Kepa Arrizabalaga, deputising for the injured David Raya, struggled to deal with high balls. Dortmund's main route forward was down the right. Half of their attacks came down that side, through Ryerson and Gadou, attacking the space Hincapie left behind when he pushed on. top.title: Arteta backs 'brilliant' Gyokeres after Arsenal waste chances to beat Dortmund
top.description: Arsenal striker Viktor Gyokeres in action against Borussia Dortmund (Ben Stansall) Mikel Arteta defended Viktor Gyokeres after the inconsistent Arsenal striker's "unbelievable" strike was followed by a costly miss in Tuesday's 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League. Arteta had urged Gyokeres to seize his opportunity after selecting the Sweden striker instead of Kai Havertz for the league phase tie at the Emirates Stadium. Initially, Gyokeres looked like doing just that with his first goal at home this season, and only his third for the Gunners in all competitions. But the 28-year-old has been much-maligned for his erratic displays since arriving from Sporting Lisbon in 2025. And he gave more ammunition to his critics when he missed a golden opportunity to seal the points with a woeful header in the closing stages. Leaping to Gyokeres's defence, Arteta said: "He had a brilliant performance today. He scored an unbelievable goal. He has the quality to do that. "What I loved the most was how connected he was to the team. We used him many times in different ways, his link-up play, the way he held the ball. "He got behind and stretched the pitch. There was a lot to like in that performance." Arsenal are unbeaten in their last 11 games in all competitions, but this was not a vintage display by the English champions, who failed to win at home for the first time this season. Arteta disagreed, insisting Arsenal were deserving of all three points on the balance of play. "The way we played, there is no question how superior, how dominant, how much of a threat we were. It was great to watch. It was unbelievable that sometimes the ball didn't go in the back of the net," he said. "The execution can be better, we rushed a little bit. Certainly we could have finished the actions better today. "There is an element of luck, how the hell some of those balls didn't go in, I don't know. There is an element of us needing to finish the actions better." - 'Courageous' - Arsenal sit fifth in the league phase with three wins and two draws from their five matches, while seventh-placed Dortmund are one point behind them. Arteta will hope for a much more ruthless display in a significant Premier League showdown with spluttering title rivals Manchester City in north London on Sunday. "What the team has shown today is a step in the right direction. There is a lot to like but obviously we want to win every game," he said. Dortmund had equalised through Maximilian Beier prior to Gyokeres's key miss. The Bundesliga leaders were well worth a point for their gritty display and boss Niko Kovac said: "This is a big one for all of us, the players, the fans and the club -- a big point away to Arsenal. "In the first 15 minutes we didn't play the way I hoped. We were too passive. "We were more courageous and pressed more actively after the break. We got Arsenal into difficult situations. "We came back because of our huge desire. I'm really happy for the boys." smg/bsp

top.title: 3 takeaways from No. 19 BYU’s loss to Ole Miss at the Maui Invitational
top.description: BYU forward Bruce Branch III drives against Mississippi forward Santiago Trouet during game at the Southwest Maui Invitational, Tuesday, Nov. 24, 2026, in Lahaina, Hawaii. | Matthew Thayer, Associated Press LAHAINA, Hawaii — Trouble in paradise for BYU. After leading Ole Miss by 14 points at halftime, the Cougars suffered a collapse of epic proportions in the second half, ultimately falling 73-63 to the Rebels Tuesday afternoon in the Maui Invitational’s second round. It’s the first loss of the season for BYU, which will now play either Arizona or Providence in the tournament’s third-place game Wednesday. Final from Maui pic.twitter.com/jZlRtOAQZ7 — BYU Men's Basketball (@BYUMBB) November 24, 2026 3 takeaways BYU’s best half of the season was followed by its worst. Playing without Rob Wright III, the Cougars were excellent in the first 20 minutes, scoring 1.2 points per possession and holding Ole Miss to just 36% shooting. BYU led by as many as 18 points before halftime and went into the break with a 14-point advantage, seemingly on its way to Wednesday’s Maui championship game. But Ole Miss came out of the locker room a completely different beast. The much-vaunted Rebel defense terrorized BYU throughout the final frame, forcing 15 turnovers and scoring 21 points in transition. Ole Miss opened the second half on a 17-0 run to quickly erase BYU’s 14-point lead. The Cougars shot just 5 of 20 after halftime, and in one 15-minute span made just two field goals. BYU desperately missed Wright, who could have provided greater ball security and general stability for the offense. But considering the Cougars got off to the start they did without Wright, they should have been able to finish without him as well. A loss like this should sting for a while, but BYU needs a quick flush with another game 24 hours away. Collin Chandler carried the Cougars. BYU’s junior guard continued his strong Maui showing with a career-high 34 points, including 21 in the first half. Chandler shot 9 of 18 from the field, 3 of 6 from deep and grabbed eight rebounds, swiping a pair of steals defensively as well. In the second half, the bulk of BYU’s offense came from Chandler free throws, as he went 9 for 10 from the charity stripe after halftime and 13 for 14 on the day. In Wright’s absence, Chandler has risen to the occasion as BYU’s top scoring option. Unfortunately for the Cougars, no one else was able to give Chandler much help on Tuesday, as his teammates shot a collective 11 for 38 (29%) and coughed up 19 turnovers. Mahomes was aboard the team’s float and even delivered a victory speech in front of the rowdy crowd. top.title: Half of NASA's aging Mars fleet knocked offline by technical issues
top.description: Two of NASA's four missions operating at Mars have suspended science operations after encountering separate technical issues in recent weeks. The missions affected by the outages — hopefully temporary — are NASA's Perseverance rover and Odyssey orbiter. Both are operating beyond their original design lifetimes. Perseverance is in its sixth year exploring the surface of Mars, having collected rock and soil samples for eventual return to Earth. The rover is now studying the rim of a crater that once contained an ancient lake of liquid water. Odyssey arrived in orbit around Mars in 2001, and is the longest-lived Mars mission in history. Losing its voice The problem on Perseverance stems from the rover's communications system. The rover has two redundant UHF radios for high-rate communications with a fleet of orbiters that relay data to Earth. A separate X-band system is available for direct-to-Earth communications at a lower data rate. Read full article Comments

top.title: We have to stay positive, urges Haaland
top.description: We have to stay positive, urges Haaland Erling Haaland has called for everyone associated with City to remain upbeat following our 2-2 UEFA Champions League draw with Napoli on Tuesday night. Match Report City hit back twice to share the spoils with Napoli Rasmus Højlund opened the scoring for the visitors at the Etihad Stadium after 55 minutes, before Ayyoub Bouaddi smashed in his first goal for City to level. Noa Lang struck the Italian side back ahead before Rayan Cherki drilled us level with four minutes left to play. The draw means Enzo Maresca’s side have one win in our last five matches across all competitions but Haaland, who captained City on the night, has believes a positive mindset will prove to be the best way to bring out the quality of everyone in the squad. “Football is so easy and so difficult,” he said after the draw. “When you win games everything is easy and you know what to do, and when you don’t win you start to question everything. The perfect thing to do is don’t think. “We have so much quality so it’s about getting that quality out of every single player. “We have to regroup, stay positive, bring all the energy on the pitch and try to do the best we can. “We missed a goal. In the end we tried to push but we couldn’t. It’s not good enough. We let them in too easy and we were not able to control and attack the game as we want.” Men's Team Cherki calls for more following Napoli draw Our next assignment on Sunday comes at the Emirates Stadium as we travel to face league-leaders Arsenal in the Premier league. Our prolific striker know exactly what is required if we are to come away with a positive result against Mikel Arteta’s side. “We go to the champions, it’s the most difficult game of the season, the champions away,” he continued. “We need a top performance from every single one of us. It’s always good to play against the best teams. “Arsenal have been the best team last year, and one of the best in the last five years now. It’s always fun to play and it’s always fun to play against Gabriel.”

top.title: Rasmus Hojlund marks goal against Manchester City with provocative celebration
top.description: Rasmus Hojlund celebrated his opening goal in Napoli ’s 2-2 draw with Manchester City with a provocative gesture towards the home fans, telling them, “There’s only one club in Manchester”. The Dane drilled a fine low finish past City keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma in the 55th minute of Tuesday night’s Champions League group stage encounter. But City twice came from behind to rescue a point , with Ayyoub Bouaddi and Rayan Cherki scoring for the home side either side of Noa Lang’s crisp volley. After breaking the deadlock Hojlund celebrated in front of the home fans, holding up one finger and saying, “There’s only one club in Manchester”, having spent two seasons at Manchester United before joining Napoli. He explained the celebration in an interview on TNT Sports afterwards: “Some good banter, there’s the rivalry between Manchester City and Man United and I obviously have a past in Manchester United, so that’s my club - nothing against Man City, but United is my club.” Asked whether it meant more to score at the Etihad , he said: “Yeah, good to score here, a good point, so happy for that.” Hojlund swapped Atalanta for Old Trafford in a £72m move in 2023, but was loaned to Napoli after two seasons, having underwhelmed in a particularly difficult second year at the club in which he endured a 21-game goalless run. He scored 26 goals in 95 appearances. The 23-year-old then completed a £38m move to the Serie A side this summer, with Napoli obliged to buy him permanently after qualifying for the Champions League. Napoli appeared much the happier side after their draw with City despite twice surrendering the lead, with the hosts having won only once in their past seven games in all competitions. Hojlund added: “I wouldn’t say it was a free game but it’s one of those were you go, OK, let’s see if we can get something. And actually I’m a bit gutted because we could probably have got all three points today.”

top.title: Greg Sankey Sends Strong Message to LSU as SEC Showdown Takes Dramatic Turn
top.description: Oct 14, 2026; Birmingham, AL, USA; SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey speaks during the SEC Basketball Tipoff at Grand Bohemian Hotel Mountain Brook. Mandatory Credit: Butch Dill-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) BATON ROUGE, La. — The Southeastern Conference has sent a powerful message to LSU as tensions between the two sides continue to escalate. What began as a disagreement over athlete eligibility has become a legal battle involving conference authority, university leadership and the future of one of college football’s most recognizable programs. Now, the SEC is preparing to consider a response that would have seemed almost unthinkable just a few months ago. SEC takes extraordinary step against LSU The SEC announced Monday that its presidents and chancellors will meet Dec. 3 to consider terminating LSU’s conference membership. The development follows an amended federal lawsuit involving LSU’s handling of athletes who previously signed professional contracts. According to The Associated Press, the conference intends to consider LSU’s removal even if the university continues to keep basketball player RJ Luis Jr. off the court. Expelling LSU would require approval from two-thirds of the SEC’s 16 university presidents and chancellors. That means at least 11 votes would be necessary. No final decision has been announced. Nevertheless, the meeting represents an extraordinary escalation in the dispute. Why the conference is taking action The conflict began earlier this fall when LSU explored adding former professional football players Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris. Both had previously signed NFL contracts, creating eligibility questions under SEC rules. LSU ultimately decided against playing either athlete. However, another disagreement emerged when the Tigers’ men’s basketball program used RJ Luis Jr., who had previously spent time with NBA organizations. Luis obtained legal protection allowing him to participate despite the conference’s objections. He subsequently appeared in LSU’s victory over Louisiana-Monroe. University president Wade Rousse later instructed basketball coach Will Wade not to play Luis again. Still, the conference argued that the situation raised serious questions about LSU’s willingness to follow its membership requirements. A dispute bigger than football The SEC’s amended complaint alleges that LSU failed to honor earlier assurances concerning conference rules. The league has also questioned whether the university demonstrated sufficient institutional control over its athletic programs. Those allegations remain part of an ongoing legal dispute. Meanwhile, LSU’s status as a founding SEC member adds another dimension to the confrontation. The Tigers have been associated with the conference since its formation in 1932. top.title: Arteta despair at Arsenal profligacy
top.description: Mikel Arteta was frustrated at the number of chances squandered by his Arsenal players - Getty Images/Richard Pelham The future Mikel Arteta may prefer to imagine for his Arsenal team is as a remorseless winning machine, although on nights such as these they continue to demonstrate an unshakeable unreliability when it comes to the main purpose of it all. There were 29 shots over the night from the English champions of which only four were on target – and in the 95th minute they were still conspiring to foul it up. This Champions League group phase game should have been decided in Arsenal’s favour within 20 minutes. It should certainly have been over by half-time. Yet from the moment Maximilian Beier scored an improbable equaliser for Borussia Dortmund on 55 minutes one was never sure Arsenal would get the goal that would win it. The leader of the Premier League against the leaders of the Bundesliga was some mismatch for long periods. Arsenal dominated and the ninth minute thump from Viktor Gyökeres that put them ahead was not even their best chance. Yet when it mattered most in the second half they struck posts and ran into a Dortmund defence that found something to hold onto and gripped for dear life. It was Gyökeres who missed one of the best chances of the second half to win the game, a header from close range that he flunked so badly that Arteta could not hide his despair. Gyökeres does occasionally, as his goal proved, look the part - and yet at other times he looks nothing like it. Still, in fifth place in the league phase table, results such as these are by no means a crisis. top.title: Best defender in the World? Upamecano sends confident message ahead of UCL clash against Lille
top.description: Best defender in the World? Upamecano sends confident message ahead of UCL clash against Lille Dayot Upamecano is looking forward to a special Champions League encounter when Bayern Munich take on Lille on Wednesday. The French defender has fond memories of the region, having spent part of his youth at Valenciennes. "It's a very special game for me. I was in Valenciennes, and Lille was like the north derby for me. I'm very happy to play here," Upamecano said at Tuesday's press conference. The 28-year-old has also earned plenty of recognition for his performances this season, with some going as far as calling him the best defender in the world . However, Upamecano was quick to remain modest when asked about the label. "Well, best defender in the world? That's an honour, but it's also kind of a big statement. I'm trying my very best. I work with my teammates and also with the coach. I just want to win every game that we play, and I'm fully focused on tomorrow's game." The defender also spoke about Jamal Musiala, who is working his way back to full fitness. Upamecano is delighted to have the attacking midfielder as a teammate rather than an opponent. "Jamal is there. He's very, very difficult to play against. In training, he always gives 100%. I'm glad to be playing alongside him. It's much, much better than having him as an opponent." Bayern are dealing with several injury problems ahead of the trip to Lille, but Upamecano is confident that the squad has enough quality to cope with the absences. “It's quite a challenging period. But we have a very strong squad, and also the players that haven't played that much over the last couple of weeks and months will show up, I'm sure, and as a team, we will do our very best, and we will help each other.” There was also a lighter moment when Upamecano was asked whether Vincent Kompany had considered using him as a striker, given that he played up front during his youth. "[laughs] Yes, when I was young, I played up front. I scored a lot of goals back then, but not so many now. I don't know, you'll have to ask the coach who will play up front tomorrow. I don't know."

nigeria.title: Political Signals: The Price Of Participation
nigeria.description: Deadly violence in Delta sharpens the question of campaign safety, while economic policy and electoral preparations face tests. An election campaign should ask citizens for their votes. In Uduere, Delta State, families are now mourning people who went to a political gathering. Police said on Tuesday that six people died in Monday’s violence at a campaign event in Ughelli North. That preliminary figure is higher than the four deaths initially reported by Ovie Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation. The circumstances and responsibility remain under investigation. This is the most consequential political development since Friday. Its significance extends beyond one party’s campaign. Every attack raises a question for the next person considering attending a meeting, volunteering or accompanying a candidate: is participation worth the risk? When citizens begin making that calculation, electoral competition has already suffered. Delta Needs Evidence And Accountability Delta Governor Sheriff Oborevwori The NDC has alleged official complicity. The Delta State Government has rejected attempts to link Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to the violence, condemned the killings and promised that those responsible will face justice. Those competing positions must remain distinct from investigative findings. The state has imposed a daily 6 p.m. to 6 a.m. curfew across Ughelli North. Restoring calm is an immediate necessity. business.title: Anchorage Digital Sets Up Asset Manager to Offer Bitcoin Yield to Clients
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Anchorage Digital Sets Up Asset Manager to Offer Bitcoin Yield to Clients Anchorage Digital, the first federally chartered crypto bank in the U.S., is moving into asset management with a new subsidiary that will offer custody clients a way to earn yield on their bitcoin. The unit, called 61st Parallel Asset Management, is expected to start operating by early December, CEO Nathan McCauley said in an interview to CoinDesk. Its first product will be a bitcoin-denominated fund, meaning returns are measured in BTC rather than dollars. The name nods to the city of Anchorage, Alaska, which sits at 61 degrees north latitude. “We have increasingly heard clients say they want to earn on top of the assets they hold at Anchorage — something that’s very common among the large financial institutions of the world,” McCauley said. Anchorage has filed a Form ADV, the disclosure document investment advisers use to register with the Securities and Exchange Commission or state regulators, or to report as exempt advisers. The form covers a firm’s ownership, business, assets under management, fees and conflicts of interest. As of Tuesday afternoon, the SEC’s public adviser database showed no record for 61st Parallel, so the filing’s details were not yet public. Paperwork dating back to summer The entity itself is not new. New York state records show that 61st Parallel Asset Management LLC, a Delaware company, registered to do business in New York on July 8, listing an office on Park Avenue South in Manhattan. Anchorage already lets clients earn on some holdings. Its website lists staking, which pays rewards for helping secure proof-of-stake networks, and a separate rewards product for eligible assets. Bitcoin runs on proof-of-work and cannot be staked natively. Anchorage has not said publicly how the fund will generate yield, what it will charge or which clients will qualify. Those details matter to bitcoin holders, because bitcoin pays no interest on its own. Common ways to earn on it include lending coins out, posting them as collateral or selling options against them, and each carries its own risk. Public companies have already tested some of those approaches. Trump Media disclosed this month that it had pledged about 73% of its bitcoin to an options program in which the counterparty can rehypothecate, or reuse, the coins. From custodian to full-service bank Founded in 2017, Anchorage received a national trust bank charter from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency in January 2021, the first crypto firm to win one. The OCC lifted a 2022 consent order over the bank’s anti-money laundering controls in August 2025. The bank no longer stands alone. Last December, the OCC granted conditional approvals to five more digital asset firms, including Circle, Ripple, BitGo, Paxos and Fidelity Digital Assets, to become national trust banks. entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. That prompted a logical - if slightly uncomfortable - follow-up question: How could he be among the league's best at his position if his own coaches didn't think he was one of the top two safeties on the roster? Brown didn't hesitate: "It's going to make sense one day." At the time, Brown sounded delusional. At the moment, he's looking prescient. After being benched in each of the previous two seasons, the 2023 third-round pick is enjoying a career-best year in which he ranks ninth among NFL safeties who have played at least 300 snaps, according to Pro Football Focus' grading system. sports.description: UTSA Roadrunners head coach Jeff Traylor looks on during the first quarter against the Rice Owls in Houston, Texas, Saturday, Oct., 3, 2026. (Zach Del Bello/San Antonio Express-News) Texas A&M did Jeff Traylor a favor. Three years ago, the Aggies interviewed him for an office that eventually makes every occupant miserable, then offered it to Mike Elko instead. Sure, the money would have been nice. But as you watch the men on the sidelines in College Station and San Antonio this Friday, ask yourself: Would you rather have Elko's options right now, or Traylor's? In some ways, they're still in completely different college football worlds. The same day that close to 110,000 people will file into Kyle Field to watch Elko's Aggies try to knock off No. 5 Texas, UTSA will be ecstatic to draw a crowd a third of that size to its regular-season finale at the Alamodome. But that disparity in attention comes with a disparity in expectations, and one of A&M's biggest problems is that it's never figured out the right ratio of the latter to the former. It's been almost three decades since the Aggies last won a conference championship, and 16 years since they've even played for one, and still every time they fall short of contention, it's a crisis. Setting high standards for your coaches is great. But once a fifth or sixth accomplished coach in a row fails to meet them, it might be fair to wonder if there's a difference between what your donor base calls standards and what outsiders call pipe dreams. It's not that coaches can't win at A&M. Kevin Sumlin and Jimbo Fisher managed one Top 5 finish apiece during their six-year tenures, and Elko came close last season. With the Aggies' money, resources and recruiting base, their competitive ceiling remains undeniably high. Their competitive floor, though, is lower than they ever like to acknowledge, and that was true even before a move to the Southeastern Conference made that more obvious. R.C. Interim boss Ashley Williams led Swansea for the second time as they were beaten 2-1 at Middlesbrough on Tuesday. Icelander Alexandersson, 44, has only been in charge of Rosenborg since June. The Norwegian top-flight club were in relegation danger when he was appointed, but lie fourth with just three games remaining in the season, which concludes in mid-December. Alexandersson previously worked for another Norwegian side, Brann, but was sacked earlier this year after 15 months in charge. On paper, the hosts were dominant. They had 63% of the ball, took 30 shots worth 2.34 expected goals (xG) and had 56 touches inside the Dortmund box. Yet both sides created four big chances, both had four shots on target, and Dortmund were the better team for long spells after the break. Viktor Gyokeres' long-range opener rewarded Arsenal's fast start, but Maximilian Beier's equaliser, made by a surging run from centre-back Joane Gadou, showed exactly where Arsenal were vulnerable. Arsenal's tactical setup Mikel Arteta lined up in a 4-2-3-1, with Declan Rice and Myles Lewis-Skelly in midfield behind Noni Madueke, Martin Odegaard and Christos Tzolis, and Gyokeres leading the line. Arsenal flew out of the blocks. Their press gave Dortmund no time on the ball in the opening 15 minutes, they completed 91% of their passes in the first half, and the opener arrived in the 10th minute when Madueke laid the ball into the path of Gyokeres, who sent a dipping 25-yard strike past Gregor Kobel. The right flank was Arsenal's main source of creativity. Madueke repeatedly got the better of Daniel Svensson , and he and Odegaard became the first Arsenal pair on record to create four or more chances each in a Champions League first half. On the other side, Piero Hincapie pushed high from left-back, joining attacks and even arriving at the back post for a header that Kobel saved early in the second half. sports.title: Arteta backs 'brilliant' Gyokeres after Arsenal waste chances to beat Dortmund
sports.description: Arsenal striker Viktor Gyokeres in action against Borussia Dortmund (Ben Stansall) Mikel Arteta defended Viktor Gyokeres after the inconsistent Arsenal striker's "unbelievable" strike was followed by a costly miss in Tuesday's 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League. Arteta had urged Gyokeres to seize his opportunity after selecting the Sweden striker instead of Kai Havertz for the league phase tie at the Emirates Stadium. Initially, Gyokeres looked like doing just that with his first goal at home this season, and only his third for the Gunners in all competitions. But the 28-year-old has been much-maligned for his erratic displays since arriving from Sporting Lisbon in 2025. And he gave more ammunition to his critics when he missed a golden opportunity to seal the points with a woeful header in the closing stages. Leaping to Gyokeres's defence, Arteta said: "He had a brilliant performance today. He scored an unbelievable goal. He has the quality to do that. "What I loved the most was how connected he was to the team. We used him many times in different ways, his link-up play, the way he held the ball. "He got behind and stretched the pitch. There was a lot to like in that performance." Arsenal are unbeaten in their last 11 games in all competitions, but this was not a vintage display by the English champions, who failed to win at home for the first time this season. Arteta disagreed, insisting Arsenal were deserving of all three points on the balance of play. "The way we played, there is no question how superior, how dominant, how much of a threat we were. It was great to watch. It was unbelievable that sometimes the ball didn't go in the back of the net," he said. "The execution can be better, we rushed a little bit. Certainly we could have finished the actions better today. "There is an element of luck, how the hell some of those balls didn't go in, I don't know. There is an element of us needing to finish the actions better." - 'Courageous' - Arsenal sit fifth in the league phase with three wins and two draws from their five matches, while seventh-placed Dortmund are one point behind them. Arteta will hope for a much more ruthless display in a significant Premier League showdown with spluttering title rivals Manchester City in north London on Sunday. "What the team has shown today is a step in the right direction. There is a lot to like but obviously we want to win every game," he said. Dortmund had equalised through Maximilian Beier prior to Gyokeres's key miss. The Bundesliga leaders were well worth a point for their gritty display and boss Niko Kovac said: "This is a big one for all of us, the players, the fans and the club -- a big point away to Arsenal. "In the first 15 minutes we didn't play the way I hoped. We were too passive. "We were more courageous and pressed more actively after the break. We got Arsenal into difficult situations. sports.description: Rasmus Hojlund celebrated his opening goal in Napoli ’s 2-2 draw with Manchester City with a provocative gesture towards the home fans, telling them, “There’s only one club in Manchester”. The Dane drilled a fine low finish past City keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma in the 55th minute of Tuesday night’s Champions League group stage encounter. But City twice came from behind to rescue a point , with Ayyoub Bouaddi and Rayan Cherki scoring for the home side either side of Noa Lang’s crisp volley. After breaking the deadlock Hojlund celebrated in front of the home fans, holding up one finger and saying, “There’s only one club in Manchester”, having spent two seasons at Manchester United before joining Napoli. He explained the celebration in an interview on TNT Sports afterwards: “Some good banter, there’s the rivalry between Manchester City and Man United and I obviously have a past in Manchester United, so that’s my club - nothing against Man City, but United is my club.” Asked whether it meant more to score at the Etihad , he said: “Yeah, good to score here, a good point, so happy for that.” Hojlund swapped Atalanta for Old Trafford in a £72m move in 2023, but was loaned to Napoli after two seasons, having underwhelmed in a particularly difficult second year at the club in which he endured a 21-game goalless run. He scored 26 goals in 95 appearances. The 23-year-old then completed a £38m move to the Serie A side this summer, with Napoli obliged to buy him permanently after qualifying for the Champions League. Napoli appeared much the happier side after their draw with City despite twice surrendering the lead, with the hosts having won only once in their past seven games in all competitions. Hojlund added: “I wouldn’t say it was a free game but it’s one of those were you go, OK, let’s see if we can get something. And actually I’m a bit gutted because we could probably have got all three points today.”

sports.title: Copa America Confirmed for Return to the United States in 2028
sports.description: CONMEBOL and CONCACAF made a joint announcement today, confirming what had long been rumored, that the Copa America will return to the United States in 2028. It will be the third edition played in the United States, after the 2016 Centenario and 2024, and the second in a row hosted outside South America. In 2024, Argentina defeated Colombia in Miami to retain their title, while previously, Chile had won the 2016 edition played in the United States by defeating Argentina. Copa America Confirmed for June 2028 The 2028 edition will be played at stadiums across the United States from June 9th to July 9th, and 16 teams will be entrants. That’s the 10 teams from South America that are CONMEBOL members, and 6 more from CONCACAF. The CONCACAF entrants will be confirmed based on how teams perform in the 2027 CONCACAF Gold Cup , which is also hosted in the United States next summer. The final on July 9th lands just days before the Los Angeles Olympics open, in the one clean window of a crowded American summer. Why the United States again? Here is the answer nobody bothers to hide. More than 1.5 million fans attended the 2024 edition, and the money in the American market is money no South American host can match. The tournament has become a cash machine, and no bid from South America can compete with it. That is simply the reality of where the sport’s economy now sits. “The CONMEBOL Copa América is much more than a tournament: it is part of our identity, our history and the greatness of South American football,” CONMEBOL president Alejandro Domínguez said. “In 2028, we will once again bring that passion to the United States, reaffirming our historic partnership with CONCACAF.” The tournament was first played in 1916 and lived its entire life in South America. It will now have been staged in the United States three times in twelve years. The case is not only financial. The venues are modern, safe and high quality, the organization of events is reliable, despite the security issues at the stadium in Miami for the 2024 final, and the United States based diaspora fills stadiums for teams that would play in front of empty seats elsewhere. Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador, Peru, and Mexico all draw like home teams in American stadiums, because for millions of their fans, it is home. Concacaf president Victor Montagliani pointed to the sporting side of the deal. “After our collaboration in 2024, we are pleased to join forces again to bring the CONMEBOL Copa America to our region in 2028,” he said, adding that the agreement will give six Concacaf national teams a new opportunity to compete against some of the best in the world. technology.title: Half of NASA's aging Mars fleet knocked offline by technical issues
technology.description: Two of NASA's four missions operating at Mars have suspended science operations after encountering separate technical issues in recent weeks. The missions affected by the outages — hopefully temporary — are NASA's Perseverance rover and Odyssey orbiter. Both are operating beyond their original design lifetimes. Perseverance is in its sixth year exploring the surface of Mars, having collected rock and soil samples for eventual return to Earth. The rover is now studying the rim of a crater that once contained an ancient lake of liquid water. Odyssey arrived in orbit around Mars in 2001, and is the longest-lived Mars mission in history. Losing its voice The problem on Perseverance stems from the rover's communications system. The rover has two redundant UHF radios for high-rate communications with a fleet of orbiters that relay data to Earth. technology.description: According to internal memos reviewed by Reuters , Microsoft has declared a "Code Red" overhaul of its engineering response practices after the November 12 outage that lost access to Exchange Online, Teams, and Outlook for users worldwide. Per the memos, Microsoft 365 Core President Jason Henderson described the outage as having the most customer impact in the history of Exchange Online. In a separate memo, Henderson wrote that an urgent production fix in a recent incident took five to six days to reach worldwide saturation. Microsoft's target for its most urgent security fixes is to move from detection to safe worldwide deployment in one hour. "Needless to say, we aren't here yet," Henderson wrote. The memos, which Reuters reviewed but Microsoft has not published, outline the response to the November 12 disruption. The company's post-incident report , dated November 20, attributed the downtime to an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July, which caused lock contention in the gateway processes. A Teams traffic failover then dumped additional load onto infrastructure already under stress, as maintenance had left nearly 14 percent of gateway server capacity offline at the time of the incident. technology.title: What's going on with the Riemann hypothesis?
technology.description: Last week, news broke that a mathematician had used AI to help crack one of the biggest outstanding problems in math: a proof of the Riemann hypothesis . The news follows several other major breakthroughs in math that have either been enabled by or managed entirely by large language model-based systems, a development that has left the entire field of mathematics in a state of upset. It's too early to say much about the proof itself—mathematicians are still in the process of digesting it. But we can say a little about how the proof came about, and what it tells us about the state of math. Tackling Riemann The Riemann hypothesis dates from the mid-1800s and was formulated by (you will be surprised to learn) Bernhard Riemann. There's not an obvious way to describe the details of the actual hypothesis simply, but it has implications for the distribution of prime numbers. This gives it significance for areas ranging from number theory to cryptography. As Wikipedia accurately states, "It is considered by pure mathematicians to be one of the most important problems in the field." Read full article Comments

technology.title: 'We are not ShinyHunters,' says criminal hacking crew that looks and acts just like ShinyHunters
technology.description: Inception, a new data theft and extortion gang that security researchers have theorized is a rebrand of the ShinyHunters group, “reject[s] this attribution” and claims it has no affiliation with any prior cybercrime enterprise. In a lengthy statement posted Tuesday and shared on X, the extortionists insist that they are a new group, with new operators, and that their alleged social engineering attacks aren’t copying anyone - but rather just abusing the weakest link in an organization’s security: “a human being holding a phone.” The rant follows a Monday report by Okta Threat Intelligence - along with social media speculation since Inception’s inception last week - that the newly emerged group is very likely ShinyHunters with a different name . Okta’s researchers based their analysis on the two groups’ shared infrastructure, plus Inception’s nearly identical tactics: voice phishing , during which the scammers trick targets into entering credentials into phishing pages and approving multi-factor authentication (MFA) requests. Inception apparently took offense to this. “We would like to address this once, clearly, and only once,” the crims' statement says. “We are not ShinyHunters. We were never ShinyHunters. We are Inception.” The gang argues that its overlapping domain registrars, hosting providers, and DNS services don’t prove anything. These are commodity services, “available to anyone who can pay for them,” Inception wrote. Plus, their similar methodologies don't necessarily make Inception a reboot. “That is not theft of tradecraft,” they wrote. “It is acknowledgment of a good idea – the same way every group after LockBit used a leak site, and nobody called them LockBit.” “Inception is a new group, with new operators, our own objectives, and our own name,” the statement continues. “What we share with the past is plumbing.” To be fair, the new crime crew has every reason to distance itself from ShinyHunters. That gang’s September FBI hack - plus several earlier digital heists during which the criminals stole information belonging to millions of people, including cancer patients , university and K-12 students - put a massive target on its collective backs. And while at least three ShinyHunters suspects were arrested in September and October, there's no confirmation that authorities have dismantled the entire operation. Plus, as a ShinyHunters spokesperson told The Register in an earlier interview, they and others in the crew started off as GnosticPlayers before rebranding as ShinyHunters in 2020 - so a reboot isn’t beyond the realm of possibility. Inception, for its part, says it “will not comment further on the ghost of ShinyHunters,” and it has its own work to do. And by work, it means copying ShinyHunters' playbook, stealing corporate data, and extorting victim companies for massive sums of money.®

technology.title: How brewers can protect beers from smoke-tainted hops
technology.description: The 2020 Oregon wildfires burned over 1 million acres, destroyed thousands of structures, and killed 11 people. Smoke from the fires spread across the entire region; this "smoke taint" adversely affected not only local wine production , but also hops grown for beer brewing. Since the Pacific Northwest produces more than 95 percent of US hops and about 40 percent of the global supply, the potential economic impact is significant. That's why Oregon State University (OSU) scientists have been studying how brewers could offset the negative impacts of smoke taint while still incorporating affected hops in their brews. Most recently, they found that it all depends on the quantity of tainted hops that are included and when hops are added during the brewing process, according to a new paper published in the Journal of the American Society of Brewing Chemists. As previously reported , the chemistry of brewing beer is a very active area of research. For instance, in 2018 , OSU chemist Thomas Shellhammer—who also co-authored this latest paper— identified the growing popularity of " dry hopping " (adding hops after fermentation, common for pale ales) among craft brewers as the likely culprit of the exploding beer bottle phenomenon. science.title: SpaceX launches secretive spy satellites from California for US Space Force (video)
science.description: null SpaceX launched another classified mission for the U.S. Space Force (USSF) today (Nov. 24), sending an unknown payload toward orbit from California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base's Space Launch Complex-4E at TK11:08 a.m. ET (1508 GMT) , carrying the U.S. Space Force's USSF-266 mission. It was the fourth mission SpaceX has launched for the military branch this month. While details about the mission's payload weren't disclosed, it's the fifth space launch in support of U.S. national security in the last two weeks, and comes amid efforts by the Space Force to expand its communications and tracking capabilities. (Image credit: SpaceX) About two and a half minutes after liftoff, Falcon 9's first-stage booster separated from the rocket's upper stage, which continued toward low Earth orbit with the classified payload. The booster, meanwhile, began a descent toward SpaceX's Of Course I Still Love You droneship in the Pacific Ocean, where it touched down approximately eight and a half minutes after launch. Tuesday's launch marked the 29th flight for this Falcon 9 booster, B1081, which previously launched NASA 's Crew-7 astronaut mission to the International Space Station , the PACE and EarthCARE science satellites , two other classified Space Force launches (USSF-153 and USSF-481), and 16 Starlink missions. Previous classified Space Force launches have fueled speculation about the possible deployment of SpaceX's Starshield satellites, which are designed for national security applications. Starshield is an adapted spacecraft design developed from SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation that supports military operations with capabilities like Earth observation and secure communications. SpaceX has not confirmed whether USSF-266 is carrying Starshield spacecraft. USSF-266 follows three other classified Space Force missions launched by SpaceX from Vandenberg earlier this month: USSF-432 on Nov. 6, USSF-627 on Nov. 11 and USSF-317 on Nov. 20, as well as a National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) launch, NROL-136, on Nov. 22. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 24, 1947: The US Navy launches the 1st Aerobee sounding rocket, but it didn't reach space
science.description: null On Nov. 24, 1947, the U.S. Navy launched the first Aerobee rocket into the sky, but it never reached space. Aerobee was a suborbital sounding rocket designed to study Earth's atmosphere . After World War 2, the United States started reusing erman V-2 rockets for this kind of research. When they started running out of V-2 rockets , the United States constructed its own rockets that were similar but cheaper to build and to launch. In the weeks leading up to the first Aerobee mission, three test flights were launched. Those tests used a dummy version of Aerobee with a live booster to see if the two stages would separate properly. On Aerobee's first real flight, the rocket flew about 35 miles high. That's below the 62-mile (100 kilometers) upper limit for the boundary of space . (NASA and the U.S. military typically consider 50 miles the edge of space.) Mission control cut the flight short after about 30 seconds, because Aerobee started to yaw, and they wanted to keep it from going completely out of control. The first Aerobee sounding rocket launched on Nov. 24, 1947 under a project led by the U.S. Navy. (Image credit: U.S. Navy) Why it mattered Billed as the " most successful sounding rocket of the space age ," the initial Aerobee rocket was suborbital rocket designed to launch experment payload of up to 100 pounds (45 kilograms) to an altitude of 75 miles (121 kilometers) or so. "The Aerobee was designed to carry instruments aloft to collect data on the upper atmosphere and to place small animals in a weightless condition for physiological studies," the U.S. National Museum of the United States Air Force wrote in a mission overview . "It was launched by a solid-propellant booster engine of 18,000 pounds thrust that burned for only two and a half seconds." An Aerobee suborbital sounding rocket of the type designed to study Earth's atmosphere. (Image credit: NMMSH) While the first Aerobee rocket did not reach space , many more made successful launches in the decades that followed. Engineers made a steady stream of upgrades to the the Aerobee rocket, allowing to fly higher and launch heavier payloads into space. It was an Aerobee rocket that launched two Phillipine monkeys on a mission to study how the effects of rapid launch acceleration might affect their bodies, an experiment that was among the frst human physiology tests that paved the way for human spaceflight . More than 1,000 Aerobee rockets have launched since then, and the last one flew in January of 1985. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

science.title: Teams Lock in Mission Architecture for NASA’s SR-1 Freedom
science.description: 5 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) NASA’s Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom, the first fission-powered spacecraft to travel beyond Earth orbit, cruises past Mars in this artist’s concept, demonstrating nuclear electric propulsion in deep space. Credit: NASA/Jonathan North NASA completed a major review for Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom and locked in key elements of the spacecraft, which is targeted to launch in 2028 and demonstrate nuclear electric propulsion in deep space for the first time. Experts from across the agency, the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), and industry met at NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland for a major SR-1 mission design review in October. Several key decisions were made, propelling the mission from an early concept toward a defined spacecraft design. “SR-1 marks a pivotal step in how we travel through the solar system,” said Steve Sinacore, SR-1 Freedom program director. “This mission will be the first freight run on the railroad of the solar system, and the decisions we’re making now are laying the tracks for every nuclear-powered spacecraft that follows.” Planned for launch in late 2028, SR-1 will use both nuclear and solar power to deliver SkyFall , a capsule carrying three next-generation helicopters, to Mars. Once deployed, the helicopters will study Martian geology and climate history, explore new terrain, and search for signs of subsurface ice. As NASA prepares for more ambitious exploration missions, future spacecraft and surface operations will require significantly more power than current systems can provide, particularly in environments where sunlight is limited or unavailable. SR-1 will demonstrate how fission power can enable long-duration missions, pave the way for reliable surface power systems to support NASA’s future Moon Base , and enable exploration deeper into the solar system. Key design decisions The SR-1 Freedom spacecraft design has evolved since NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman first introduced the concept in March at the agency’s Ignition event, where leadership shared plans to develop a fission-powered spacecraft in time for the next Mars launch window. One significant change is to use a shorter boom than the one shown in early illustrations. The boom separates the reactor from the spacecraft’s main body, known as the Power and Propulsion Element. The shorter boom will reduce weight, simplify assembly, and help streamline the spacecraft’s design. Planned for launch in late 2028, Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom will use both nuclear and solar power to deliver SkyFall to Mars. This infographic explains the components of the spacecraft. Credit: NASA/David Lam NASA and DOE experts also determined that improvements in shielding and spacecraft design will allow the reactor to operate closer to the rest of the spacecraft. This will simplify integration while maintaining the radiation protection needed for spacecraft electronics and the SkyFall payload.

science.title: 1st-ever detection of a dying star's 'final nuclear heartbeat' challenges what we know about our sun's eventual death
science.description: null As ubiquitous as the sun is to us today, our star is not eternal; one day, albeit in billions of years, it will die. While massive stars die in supernova explosions, the sun and stars of similar mass die quieter deaths. But that doesn't mean these stars completely go out with a whimper. New observations collected using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), the world's largest radio telescope comprised of 66 antennas in northern Chile, reveal that the sun's death throes may be different from what scientists had initially believed. NASA Jet Propulsion Lab (JPL) researcher Raghvendra Sahai, who led the investigation, explained the shape the ALMA observations took: "It's essentially a physical snapshot of an event that, until now, we've mostly inferred from theoretical models. We've caught, for the first time, a star's final nuclear heartbeat, frozen in gas." Sun-like stars "die" when they run out of hydrogen in their cores. This means that the fusion of hydrogen to helium ceases in the stellar core, and because this nuclear process is a star's main energy source, the star no longer has the outward push to support itself against the inward push of its own gravity. As the star's core collapses to create a stellar remnant called a white dwarf , the outer layers where hydrogen is still fusing to form helium swell out. This expansion leads to a relatively short-lived " red giant " phase. Eventually, these outer layers will cool and disperse, leaving the central white dwarf surrounded by a so-called "planetary nebula" shell of debris. During the red giant phase, as the stellar core is surrounded by shells of hydrogen and helium, these layers are occasionally rocked by flares in nuclear activity called thermal pulses. During these episodes, stellar material is flung into space. To better understand this phase in stellar evolution, the team focused ALMA on a star called IRAS 06530-0213, located around 12,000 light-years away in the constellation Monoceros. This revealed a giant ring of gas that appears to be a frozen fossil of the star's last thermonuclear flare-up. This thermonuclear fossil rings an hourglass-shaped planetary nebula in the act of forming. "Most of us think of stars as unchanging points of light, but this is a real-time snapshot of a star's death throes," Sahai said. "It's the brief, violent transition between a bloated red giant and a glowing planetary nebula, frozen mid-action." ALMA image of IRAS 06530-0213, revealing a giant ring of molecular gas surrounding a young, hourglass-shaped nebula. (Image credit: ALMA (ESO/NAOJ/NRAO); Sahai et al. It represents the first direct evidence of the last thermal pulse before this kind of star enters the final phase of its life. science.title: NASA’s Titan-Bound Dragonfly Rotorcraft Gets Its Eyes
science.description: Science instruments for NASA’s Dragonfly are starting to arrive at the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory (APL) in Laurel, Maryland, where the car-sized rotorcraft is coming together for its mission to explore Saturn’s largest moon, Titan. From left, technicians Chad Cook and Seth Harvey install the high-resolution microscopic imager – part of the seven-camera DragonCam science imaging suite – onto NASA’s Dragonfly rotorcraft at the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory (APL) in Laurel, Maryland, on Nov. 6, 2026. NASA/Johns Hopkins APL/Ed Whitman First to check in: DragonCam, which consists of seven cameras designed to characterize Titan ’s surface at multiple scales during flight and while on the ground. By mid-November, all seven cameras developed and built by Malin Space Science Systems had been installed in their insulated housings, tested, and integrated into the rotorcraft. Each camera will look out at Titan through a window in a foam enclosure that insulates the cameras and Dragonfly’s interior from Titan’s cryogenic environment, where ambient temperatures reach minus 290 degrees Fahrenheit. A configurable LED array, built at APL and spanning the light spectrum from the infrared to the ultraviolet, provides information about the color of surface materials at the sampling site and helps scientists make inferences about their composition. During Titan’s long night, which spans nearly eight Earth days, these observations also may allow DragonCam to identify organic molecules that fluoresce under ultraviolet light. The LED illumination also allows us to see Titan as human eyes would. “One of the most exciting things about Dragonfly is that we’ll be able to see Titan from perspectives we’ve never had before,” said Elizabeth Turtle, Dragonfly principal investigator at APL. “With the capability to take images when Dragonfly is on the surface as well as while flying, DragonCam will give us both detailed views and sweeping panoramas of Titan’s landscape, as well as insight into the processes that shaped this extraordinary world.
